Read the distribution map of haze areas nationwide on December 15, 2013 (Figure A) and the schematic diagram of the vertical distribution of near-surface air temperature observed 5 times at a certain place in the haze area on that day (Figure B), and complete the following questions. <image1> At what time is the near-surface air quality in the area shown in Figure B most likely to begin to improve?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure B is a schematic diagram of the vertical distribution of near-surface air temperature; the vertical axis represents height (meters), roughly from 0 to 1.6 m; the horizontal axis represents air temperature, and the arrow direction is from “low” on the left side to “high” on the right side. In the figure there are 5 vertical profiles of air temperature at different times, labeled respectively as 5:00, 20:00, 8:00, 12:00, and 15:00. Each profile shows the distribution form of air temperature near the ground changing with height. Reasoning: Near the ground, if air temperature rises as height increases, it indicates that an inversion layer exists, the lower atmosphere is stable, pollutants are not easy to disperse, and air quality is difficult to improve; if near-surface air temperature begins to decrease as height increases, it indicates that the inversion has been destroyed, convection and diffusion of lower-level air are strengthened, and air quality begins to improve. In Figure B, the near-surface profiles at 5:00, 20:00, and 8:00 still show relatively obvious inversion or stable states; by 12:00, the near-surface inversion no longer dominates, and the air temperature profile begins to show a state favorable to vertical diffusion. Therefore, the earliest time when air quality is most likely to begin improving is 12:00.

raw_record.question_text:
The formation and dissipation of haze are closely related to the stability of the lower atmosphere. Read the distribution map of haze areas nationwide on December 15, 2013 (Figure A) and the schematic diagram of the vertical distribution of near-surface air temperature observed 5 times at a certain place in the haze area on that day (Figure B), and complete the following questions.

<image1>

At what time is the near-surface air quality in the area shown in Figure B most likely to begin to improve?

method.method_draft: First describe 图乙’s axes and the five labeled temperature profiles. For each time, judge near-surface stability from the curve direction: profiles whose temperature rises with height indicate inversion/stable air, while a profile whose temperature starts to decrease with height indicates the inversion is being destroyed. The earliest labeled time in 图乙 when the near-surface inversion is no longer dominant is 12时, so that is when air quality most likely begins to improve.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图乙为近地面气温垂直分布示意图，纵轴表示高度（米），大致从0到1.6 m；横轴表示气温，箭头方向由左侧“低”到右侧“高”。图中有5条不同时刻的气温垂直廓线，分别标注为5时、20时、8时、12时、15时。各廓线显示近地面随高度变化的气温分布形态。推理：近地面若气温随高度升高而升高，说明存在逆温层，低层大气稳定，污染物不易扩散，空气质量难以好转；若近地面气温开始随高度升高而降低，说明逆温被破坏，低层空气对流和扩散增强，空气质量开始改善。图乙中，5时、20时、8时的近地面廓线仍表现出较明显的逆温或稳定状态；到12时，近地面逆温已不再占主导，气温廓线开始表现为有利于垂直扩散的状态。因此空气质量最有可能开始好转的最早时间是12时。
